claims.text: Wear resistance in high-entropy-alloy coatings is controlled by a strain-induced phase transformation at the sliding interface.
The strain-induced transformed phase forms a robust protective tribolayer.
Adding Ti or a comparable element shifts the threshold for the wear-induced phase transformation.
A baseline AlCrFeNiV-like coating has a mixed microstructure.
The baseline coating has no deliberately tuned phase-transformation threshold.
Localized sliding stresses induce a phase transformation at the coating surface.
The transformed surface phase rearranges into a dense tribolayer.
The dense tribolayer resists abrasive and delamination wear.
Changing alloy composition changes the stress threshold required to trigger the transformation.
AlCrFeNiV undergoes abrasive and delamination wear during ambient-temperature sliding.
The composition modified by targeted element addition will have a lower wear rate than the baseline.
The modified coating will exhibit improved frictional behavior relative to the baseline.
Earlier or more extensive formation of the protective tribolayer causes the predicted improvement in wear and friction.
The hypothesis applies under moderate-to-high sliding stresses at ambient temperature.
Severe oxidation, extreme temperature, or large-scale segregation can dominate the wear mechanism and invalidate the proposed relationship.
Ti addition can substantially alter the phase constitution and microstructure of high-entropy alloys.
Ti is an example of an element whose large atomic radius provides the proposed transformation-threshold effect.
Large-radius alloying additions can generate atomic-level stress and promote an FCC-to-BCC transformation in high-entropy alloys.
The baseline has less effective tribolayer formation and consequently a higher wear rate.
Failure to observe both an earlier or more extensive transformation and a statistically significant wear or friction improvement would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention allows the addition to either trigger or suppress the transformation, but the predicted outcome unconditionally expects earlier or more extensive transformation and improved wear. The outcome for the suppression branch is not specified.
